matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When trying to fix the equation, first explore moving a single matchstick within the same character, because intra‑character changes often preserve surrounding symbols and avoid creating stray sticks.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of the search, before considering moves that affect other characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal within a V to turn it into an X, rather than moving that diagonal to a different character and leaving the original V with a single diagonal.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, check that each resulting character matches a known Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or an allowed operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before further reasoning.
matchstick.example: After moving a diagonal from X, the remaining single diagonal does not correspond to any Roman numeral, so the move is invalid.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A solitary diagonal stick does not form any valid Roman numeral; ensure that removing a diagonal from V or X does not leave a lone diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a diagonal stick from a V or X.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equation, then explore moving a stick from one character to another, ensuring both source and target remain valid symbols.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X to create a new V character, which leaves the original X invalid.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation after any transformation; the equality must hold.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming that all symbols are valid.
matchstick.example: Even if 'VV' were a valid numeral, you must check that its value matches the other side of the equation.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Never remove a stick from the '=' sign unless you intend to replace it with another '=', because a single horizontal line becomes a minus sign and the equation would lose its equality operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating moves that involve the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Taking a horizontal stick from '=', leaving a single line, which is a minus sign, not an equals sign.

matchstick.title: Validate whole numeral strings for proper Roman numeral syntax
matchstick.principle: After each character is valid, ensure that each multi‑character numeral obeys Roman numeral rules (no illegal repetitions, correct subtractive patterns).
matchstick.example: The string 'VV' is invalid because V cannot be repeated.

matchstick.title: Intra-character diagonal transformation (V↔X)
matchstick.principle: When a V or X appears, moving one of its diagonal sticks within the same character can change V to X or X to V, adjusting its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a multiple of 5 and a V or X is present.
matchstick.example: Changing IV to IX by moving a diagonal within the V to become an X.

matchstick.title: Transform '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick to an adjacent I
matchstick.principle: If a '+' operator is adjacent to an I, you can move the vertical stick from '+' onto the I, turning '+' into '-' and the I into a valid numeral (e.g., II).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is close and a '+' and an adjacent I are present.
matchstick.example: Turning '+ I' into '- II' by moving the vertical stick.

matchstick.title: Intra-character operator transformation (e.g., '+' → '=', '-' → '=')
matchstick.principle: Operators can be changed by rotating or repositioning a stick within the same character; for example, adding a second horizontal line to '+' makes '=', or removing the vertical line from '+' makes '-'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the operator type appears to be the only mismatch.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' by removing its vertical stick.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to search inter‑character moves first, missing simpler intra‑character fixes.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First enumerate possible intra‑character changes (e.g., V↔X) and test them before exploring inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Leaving a single angled stick after moving a diagonal from X or V (invalid numeral)
matchstick.why_it_happens: It moves a diagonal without ensuring the source character remains a valid numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After removing a diagonal, verify that the source character still forms a valid numeral; if not, discard the move.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: Focus on symbol validity but neglect the final arithmetic check.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the values of both sides after a move and confirm the equality.

matchstick.description: Accepting invalid Roman numeral strings (e.g., repeated V or illegal subtractive patterns) after a stick move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model validates characters individually but does not check the whole numeral's syntax.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After symbol validation, run a Roman numeral syntax check on each multi‑character numeral.

matchstick.description: Omitting the equality sign in the final answer
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may forget to include the equation or accidentally drop the sign while editing.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the final answer line follows the exact format 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>' and includes an '='.
